chapters.summary: This chapter declares that God has spoken through his Son in these last days, and demonstrates that Christ is far superior to the angels.
keyPoints: In former times God spoke to the fathers through the prophets in many portions and many ways; in these last days he has spoken to us through his Son.
Christ is the brightness of God's glory and the exact representation of his being, upholding all things by his power, and he purged our sins.
Christ is far superior to the angels, for he has inherited a more excellent name and is God's firstborn Son, whom all the angels are to worship.
chapters.application: When we face many competing voices in life, we should pay attention to God's revelation in Christ. Christ has already cleansed us from sin; let us hold him in reverence, honor him as supreme, and obey his word.

chapters.summary: This chapter warns believers not to neglect so great a salvation, and explains how Christ became man and suffered death to save the world, becoming a merciful and faithful high priest.
keyPoints: Believers are reminded to pay much closer attention to what they have heard, lest they drift away, for this salvation was confirmed by the Lord himself.
Christ was made lower than the angels for a little while, and because of the suffering of death was crowned with glory and honor, so that he might taste death for everyone.
Christ took on flesh and blood so that through death he might destroy the power of the devil and free those who through fear of death were subject to lifelong bondage.
chapters.application: Let us treasure the salvation we have received and not take God's work lightly. In times of hardship, let us reflect on Christ's suffering, find comfort and strength there, and press on courageously along the heavenly road.

chapters.summary: This chapter urges believers to consider Jesus as the apostle and high priest of our confession, and warns against an evil heart of unbelief, lest they fail to enter God's rest as the Israelites did in the wilderness.
keyPoints: Jesus is worthy of more glory than Moses, for he is the one who rules over God's household.
If we hold fast our original confidence firmly to the end, we share in Christ.
Do not harden your hearts, lest you be deceived by sin and, with a hardened heart, fall away from the living God.
chapters.application: Remind yourself daily that Jesus is our Savior and also our great High Priest. When your heart grows hard or you feel like giving up, exhort one another and hold fast to the Lord to the end, that you may enter his rest.

chapters.summary: This chapter urges believers to hold fast to faith and enter the rest God has promised, and emphasizes the supremacy of Christ as our high priest.
keyPoints: We are warned not to harden our hearts, but to enter God's rest today, lest anyone fall by following the example of disobedience.
The word of God is living and active, able to pierce and divide the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
Jesus, as our high priest, is able to sympathize with our weaknesses, so we should come boldly to the throne of grace.
chapters.application: When life feels busy or full of worry, remember to pause, trust in God's promises, and enter into his rest. Pray with boldness and confidence, for Christ has already accomplished everything for us.

chapters.summary: This chapter explains that Christ is a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, far greater than Aaron, and urges believers to grow toward maturity, leaving behind the elementary teachings about Christ.
keyPoints: A high priest must be able to deal gently with the ignorant and wayward, and must be called by God - and this is exactly what Christ is.
Though Christ was a Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered, and having been made perfect, became the source of eternal salvation.
Believers should leave behind the elementary teachings about Christ and press on to maturity, no longer remaining infants.
chapters.application: Let us follow Christ's example, learning obedience through hardship, and pursue growth in our spiritual life rather than remaining at the stage of new believers - training ourselves, like those who can handle solid food, to discern good from evil and live out a mature faith.

chapters.summary: This chapter urges believers to leave the elementary teachings about Christ and press on to maturity, warns of the danger of falling away from the true faith, and strengthens believers' confidence through God's promise and hope.
keyPoints: Believers are urged to leave the foundational teachings behind and press on toward maturity rather than remaining stagnant.
A warning is given to those who, having once been enlightened, fall away - it is hard for them to be renewed to repentance again, like land under a curse.
Believers are encouraged to follow the example of those who came before, who through faith and patience inherited the promises, and to hold fast to the hope set before them.
chapters.application: We should continually grow in the faith and never stagnate or fall back. God is faithful and will remember our labor; therefore let us hold fast to hope and endure to the end.

chapters.summary: This chapter explains that Jesus Christ is a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, surpassing the Levitical priesthood, and brings a better hope and a complete salvation.
keyPoints: Melchizedek prefigures Christ - without genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, resembling the Son of God, a priest forever.
The Levitical priests, because of their weakness, could not bring anything to perfection and had to be continually replaced, but Jesus was established as priest forever by an oath.
Jesus is holy, without evil, and undefiled; he offered himself once for all, accomplishing what the law could never accomplish.
chapters.application: We no longer need to draw near to God through works or rituals; we need only trust in Jesus, our high priest who lives forever and intercedes for us, and come boldly before God to receive mercy and find grace.

chapters.summary: This chapter explains that Christ is the mediator of a better covenant, whose priesthood far surpasses that of the old covenant, and cites the prophecy of Jeremiah concerning the fulfillment of the new covenant.
keyPoints: Christ is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, a minister of the true tabernacle.
The service of the earthly priests is only a shadow of the things in heaven; Christ offers a more excellent sacrifice.
God promises to establish a new covenant, forgiving sins and writing his law on people's hearts, while the old covenant is growing old and fading away.
themes: The Superiority of the New Covenant
chapters.application: Let us rely by faith on Christ our mediator, and live out a new life guided from within by God's law, no longer dependent on outward regulations, but enjoying an intimate relationship with God.

chapters.summary: This chapter contrasts the worship of the old covenant's earthly tabernacle with Christ's single offering in the heavenly Holy of Holies, showing that Christ's blood cleanses the conscience so that we may serve the living God.
keyPoints: The worship of the old covenant had many regulations, but the gifts offered could not make the worshiper's conscience perfect.
Christ, as high priest, entered the heavenly sanctuary and, through his own blood, offered himself once for all, obtaining eternal redemption.
Christ's death established the new covenant, so that those who are called might receive the promised eternal inheritance.
themes: The Shadow of the Old Covenant
The Mediator of the New Covenant
chapters.application: We no longer need to be saved by works; we need only trust in Christ's once-for-all sacrifice for sin. If you feel burdened by guilt today, come boldly before God, for his blood has already cleansed us.

chapters.summary: This chapter explains that Christ's single sacrifice is eternally effective, replacing the repeated sacrifices of the old covenant, and urges believers to persevere and hold fast to their faith without shrinking back.
keyPoints: Since the law is only a shadow of the good things to come and cannot make anyone perfect, Christ came into the world to do God's will; by offering his body once for all, he makes believers holy.

Christ offered one sacrifice for sins forever and sat down at the right hand of God, from then on waiting for his enemies to be made his footstool, for by this one sacrifice he has made those who are being sanctified perfect forever.

Believers should draw near to God with a sincere heart and in full assurance of faith, hold fast to the hope they profess, spur one another on in love, not give up meeting together, and above all not sin deliberately, knowing that the Judge is coming.
themes: Holding Fast to the Faith and Encouraging One Another
The Warning against Deliberate Sin and Apostasy
chapters.application: Since we may boldly enter the Most Holy Place through the blood of Jesus, let us draw near to God with a sincere heart and full assurance of faith, hold fast to hope, encourage one another, and not shrink back in times of trouble, for he who promised is faithful.

chapters.summary: This chapter, through the testimony of the great heroes of faith from ancient times, explains the nature and power of faith and encourages believers to hold fast to their own faith.
keyPoints: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
The people of old were commended by God through faith - men like Abel, Enoch, and Noah.
Through faith, believers endured suffering, obtained promises, and became a great cloud of witnesses.
chapters.application: In times of hardship, look to God in faith, trust in his promises, follow the example of the saints of old, run the race set before you, and glorify God.

chapters.summary: This chapter urges believers to look to Jesus, endure trials, remember that the Lord disciplines those he loves, and pursue holiness and peace.
keyPoints: Let us lay aside every weight and the sin that so easily entangles us, and run with endurance the race set before us.
The Lord disciplines those he loves, just as a father disciplines his son; discipline yields the fruit of righteousness and peace.
Be careful not to refuse him who speaks, for our God is a consuming fire; let us serve him with reverence and awe.
chapters.application: When facing life's challenges and discipline, look to Jesus, trust in the Father's love, view hardship as an opportunity for growth, pursue peace and holiness, and serve God with a thankful heart.

chapters.summary: Hebrews chapter 13 teaches believers to hold fast to virtues such as brotherly love, hospitality to strangers, and honoring marriage, and reminds us to follow Jesus' example, offering the sacrifice of praise, doing good, and sharing with others, for these are the sacrifices that please God.
keyPoints: Let brotherly love continue, and do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing so some have entertained angels without knowing it.
Honor marriage, and let the marriage bed be kept pure, for God will judge the sexually immoral.
Follow the example of Jesus - go to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore, and through him continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise.
chapters.application: Let us live with hearts full of love, be ready to welcome others, and guard the purity of marriage. Whatever circumstances we face, let us depend on the Lord and glorify God through praise and good deeds.
